data.reason: The man lifts a huge, multi-hundred-kilogram boulder overhead with one hand as if it weighed nothing, and the boulder appears out of nowhere while the stones in the pile change shape and number between frames.

The frames show a player holding a ball, then the camera tilts down to her feet standing on the court, with consistent shadows and no serve ever shown. The motion is a simple camera pan with no clear physical impossibility, though the ball held at the start simply never reappears.

The hammer rests motionless in the grass for most of the clip and is never seen being thrown. In the last frame it suddenly morphs into a different object while debris spontaneously erupts, with no impact to cause it. That is an object transforming and an effect without a cause.

The wooden plank stays in the same spot in the frame while the woman's hand, the rope and the hardware around it change shape and attachment from frame to frame. The rope morphs into a rod with a bracket, and the plank never actually slides or makes a groove, so the objects interact inconsistently.

Nothing in the frames looks like a domino chain reaction. The disc-like pieces on rods mostly stay in place while the structure shifts and morphs, and the curved bundle of rods on the left straightens and changes shape, so the objects deform in ways that don't follow any causal toppling.

The worker swings the hammer repeatedly, but it never makes visible contact with the pipe or any fitting. The hammer head blurs and morphs, and its handle seems to merge with the hand. A second hammer head lies on the floor, and the pipe never reacts to any impact. The striking action has no physical effect.

The discus rests motionless in the gravel, then suddenly lifts off with no thrower or force acting on it, leaving a dark hole-like shadow. It then reappears upright and rolling, kicking up dust. This is spontaneous motion with inconsistent shadows.

The bat vanishes partway through the swing: at 2.12 s a ball-like object appears near his shoulder and then the bat is gone entirely. His hands are left empty, and the ball on the infield sits still the whole time, never struck or rolling.

Pebbles in the gravel shift, appear and disappear between frames without clear causes. Individual rocks float in midair (around 3.38–5.12 s), drifting slowly instead of falling, and debris particles hang suspended while the slab and people stay static.

The mallet appears from nowhere as a second stick sticking out of the horse's head area, and the rider's held mallet does not connect to it. A white ball pops into existence mid-air, then sits at the horse's mouth, then floats beside it without any strike or bounce.

The brush waves around above a white object that doesn't really look like a boot, and it rarely touches it. The mud pattern stays roughly the same throughout, and the brush seems to merge with the object around 2.6–3.4 s, so the cleaning action and the object's identity are inconsistent.
The video is a nearly static shot of a patchwork-wrapped box tied with twine, with only slight camera drift and minor pattern shimmer. No implausible motion or object behavior is visible.

The finger stays in a pre-existing hole, then lifts out and leaves the indentation intact with no rebound. The hole is much wider than the finger and stays the same while the finger moves. Mostly plausible, though the hole is oddly oversized and there's no visible deformation as the finger presses.

Two jetskis carve turns that leave consistent curved white wakes, and their motion and spray look continuous and believable from frame to frame. The circular wake pattern has minor oddities but no clear physics break.

The brick floats unsupported in midair beside the wall in the early frames, hovering with nothing holding it. Later it changes size and shape and morphs into the wall, so it does not behave like a rigid object.

The bat appears to strike the bottle and shards fly, yet the bottle stays fully intact and upright, with no breakage. The bat then retreats backward, and the shards vanish, leaving only a slightly cracked surface pattern.
The metal box appears from nowhere: it isn't in the compartment early on, then is suddenly in the hand at 5.12 s. The hand also fades in and out as a ghostly blur, which breaks object permanence.

A paraglider flies steadily over a valley with the camera following behind. The wing keeps a consistent shape, and the pilot and lines stay connected throughout. The motion is smooth, with only small shifts in wing angle and background parallax.

The axe starts embedded in the post, then pulls back out and vanishes, and the post is left with no gash or split where the axe was lodged. The handle also changes shape between frames. Chips fly as if the axe were striking, yet it moves away from the post.

The video is a near-static close-up of two twine strands crossed at a knot on fabric, with only slight camera drift. Nothing moves or deforms in an impossible way. The knot's topology is a bit ambiguous, but it stays consistent across frames.

From the overhead view, the figure seems to float and spin over the concrete for six seconds without landing. Its body morphs: limbs vanish and reappear, the helmet and head shift, and the clothing colors change. No real takeoff or landing is shown.

A bowler runs toward the camera, with the camera tilting up as he approaches. His leg and stride motions look mostly natural, and no ball delivery is visible. There is some odd leg morphing: around 4.25 s the legs look tangled, and the knee pads look inconsistent. The arms and body also look a little distorted, but nothing is a clear, egregious violation.

The coin is huge in mid-air, then vanishes at 1.42 s, leaving only a faint ellipse on the ground. It then reappears hovering flat just above the concrete at 2.12 s before settling. That is inconsistent object continuity and an unnatural landing rather than a tumbling bounce.

The object in the detective's hand keeps changing: it starts as a flat dark scraper, becomes a box, then turns into a birdhouse-like object stuck high on the wall. The hidden compartment also changes shape, and the box never clearly comes out of the hole.

The wrench hovers over the pipe and never grips anything, and the pipes never come apart, so the action does nothing. The pipe also seems to shift and change shape slightly, but nothing is blatantly impossible.

The crater is already there before any impact. A ball then enters the frame and turns into a strange metal object with a handle, which is an object transformation. Cause and effect are backwards, and the ball never actually makes the crater.

The dominoes on the right shift around between frames: pieces that were lying nearly flat rise back to steeper angles, and the number of dominoes changes from about nine to seven. The leftmost domino also stays upright while the rest lean back toward it, so there is no real tipping chain reaction.

The roller moves right and paint builds up progressively as it goes, which is plausible. But the roller's frame and handle shift in odd ways between frames, and a flat painted panel appears over what was a wooden post and fence. This suggests the surface geometry is changing rather than just being coated with paint.

The die hangs tilted on one edge, apparently floating or balanced, for about 3.4 seconds without rolling. It then morphs: its shape turns into a blob and its markings change from numerals to pips. It never actually rolls across the table.

The video shows a faucet pouring a steady stream of water into a sink. The stream stays continuous and falls downward, and the camera drifts slightly. There are no clear physics violations, though the stream's texture is a bit static and smeared.

The man holds two shovels at once, and their blades seem to merge and pass through each other and the burning logs. No sand is moved, and the fire keeps burning, with flames poking through the shovel blade.

A dark axe-like blade suddenly appears inside the existing crack, stays there, then vanishes, with no visible swing or impact. The beam stays completely unchanged before and after, with no split, debris or movement.

A chef uses a peel to slide a pizza into the oven. The motion is smooth and consistent, apart from a slight shift in the peel handle's shape and minor inconsistencies in the pizza toppings, and no clear physical violation is visible.

No shot put is ever thrown or seen landing. A deep crater simply appears in the sand next to the athlete with no impact. At the end, sand erupts from the crater on its own while the man's legs dissolve into it, so the crater forms without a projectile and the body behaves unphysically.

The puck starts mid-air and tilted, then sits nearly motionless on the ice instead of sliding. When the skater passes, it tilts and lifts without clear contact, then settles flat. These are mild oddities rather than clear violations.

The player dribbles near a wall, but the ball's motion is inconsistent. In the last frame it appears to merge with or smear into his leg and hands, and it is never clearly seen bouncing off the wall. Between frames the ball seems to jump between hand positions without a plausible trajectory.

The person stands on a wooden block that sits on a rigid beam-like 'rope', which merges oddly with a real rope. The pole seems to clip through the body and harness, and the person glides forward without walking. The block moves without being pushed, and the pole never touches it.

A large ball floats in midair above the pinball playfield, changing pattern and size from frame to frame. It then drifts down and disappears without any bounce or ricochet, while other balls appear and vanish. Hovering, morphing and vanishing like this breaks physics.

A white stream from the faucet runs into a transparent cylinder that never fills or overflows and produces no bubbles. The faucet morphs and disappears, and the hand passes through and merges with the cylinder and the stream, which are inconsistent object interactions.

The gymnast slowly lowers from a handstand into a horizontal, planche-like hold supported by one hand on a pommel, with the other arm never visible. The body's centre of mass drifts far from that single support point while he stays suspended, which is not a balance a real body could hold.

The video shows a bicycle, not a unicycle. Its structure is inconsistent: the frame doesn't clearly connect the two wheels, and the wheel positions and geometry morph between frames. The rider also appears to stay on while the bike drifts toward and into the brick wall, without plausible motion or contact.

A person holds a yellow ring-like band and stretches it slightly between two hands. It deforms in a plausible way, no snap occurs, and nothing clearly impossible happens. The band behaves somewhat rigidly, but stays coherent.

The trunk shows a wide-open cut gap that never grows or closes, while the saw blade sits motionless in the gap and doesn't actually cut. The upper trunk floats separated above the lower part, and a horizontal log hovers in midair beside it, unsupported.

The scene morphs without any physical cause. White cheese held between two chopsticks turns into a yellow block of Swiss cheese, the chopsticks merge into a single knife-like utensil, and a large cheese block appears beneath it. No hole is ever poked into the cheese.

The dough floats in the air for over two seconds without falling, then at 2.88 s it splits into two separate pieces, one high in the air and one in the man's hands. Later the pieces morph into odd shapes, so object permanence and gravity are both broken.

The video shows hands crocheting a rainbow piece with a hook rather than threading a needle, but that is a prompt mismatch, not a physics problem. The crochet fabric changes shape and its colour pattern shifts noticeably between frames, the hook seems to pass through the yarn loops oddly, and the fabric morphs.

The spinner looks nearly stopped and sharp around 2.87–3.40 s, then is heavily motion-blurred again at 4.00 s, so it seems to speed up with no external input. The arms also appear to morph between frames instead of slowing steadily under friction.

No javelin is thrown. The man grips a board while objects morph: the board and its attached metal/strap parts change shape and appear and disappear, and a metal piece seems to pass through his face. Objects deform and interpenetrate in implausible ways.

The blade seems to lie on or pass into the thick stem, yet the stem never divides. Fibrous debris appears and shifts around without any real cutting progress, and the single blade merges into the stem without a matching second jaw, which is an implausible tool–object interaction.

The paddle blade starts above the water and morphs: it bends, sprays water while seemingly not entering it, then turns into a splash with the arm, and finally becomes a different yellow blade floating in the water. The object deforms and changes identity, and the water reacts inconsistently with the paddle's motion.

The paper keeps changing shape and size in ways folding can't explain. A multi-flap crane-like form at the start becomes a single thin strip by 1.75–2.62 s, then grows back into a large multi-pointed shape, so the paper appears, vanishes and reforms rather than being folded continuously.

The jeans in the drawer change shape inconsistently. The garment's volume and state appear to morph rather than follow continuous handling.

An unridden scooter drifts slowly to the right with no visible push. In the last frame a red trash can suddenly appears at the edge right next to it. There is no real collision, and the scooter never tilts. The scooter moving by itself and the trash can popping into existence are implausible.

The scene is incoherent. A hand appears from nowhere and hovers in front of the circular frames without clearly touching the mirror, and the arm's clothing and shape shift between frames. The ring structure changes geometry as the camera moves, and the reflection doesn't behave like a real mirror.

The hurdler appears to hover over the hurdles across several seconds instead of following a ballistic arc. The hurdles also shift and change in number while his legs pass through or merge with the bars, which looks physically implausible.

A welder works under a metal frame sculpture while sparks fly from the arc and light up the scene, which looks plausible. The camera moves smoothly and the structure stays mostly consistent. The welder emerges somewhat abruptly in the early frames, but no clear physics violation is visible.

The runner never actually clears any hurdles, and as the camera tracks him the surroundings change impossibly: the stadium stands and concrete structure morph into an open field with trees, and the track lanes change direction. That is a continuity break in a single continuous shot.

The skater glides and moves through arabesque/camel-like positions with plausible balance and blade contact, but the poses change somewhat abruptly between frames, with legs seeming to swap and the costume skirt morphing. There is no clear accelerating spin, and the limb continuity looks questionable.

The ball never visibly bounces off the wall; it seems to stay stuck to the player's hand, which sometimes pushes it against or into the wall. The lighting jumps abruptly as the sun appears and disappears, and the hand and ball contact looks inconsistent.

The hand touches the die and withdraws while the die stays still; its slight shift across frames matches the coaster moving too, so it is camera motion. The die never actually rolls, which is a prompt mismatch rather than a physics error.

The discus keeps changing form, from a disc to something like a rugby ball to a thin blue frisbee, and then it vanishes. The person's body also contorts impossibly: the head appears to turn backward, and one leg ends in an arm-like shape at 5.17 s. The discus is never released or seen landing, so no crater forms.

data.reason: The red sphere 'yo-yo' hangs and drifts against the wall with no real toss or bounce. Its surface pattern keeps morphing, the string appears and disappears, and the sphere seems to sink into and merge with the brick wall at times.

For several seconds the ball stays glued to the player's hand while he moves slowly toward the net. After his hands go down past the net, the ball floats up near his head, then rises and hangs in the air with no clear strike. It never moves like a ball that has been spiked.

A huge stack of papers descends from above with no visible support. It then merges into and replaces the original small stack on the desk, and that stack vanishes inside it. Objects appear, float and merge in a way that is not physically plausible.

The red tie's structure changes in ways that don't follow from the hand movements. At 0.00 s a loose end is being wrapped across, but by 0.88–1.75 s it has vanished, and later knots appear and reshape without any wrapping or threading that would produce them. Fingers also merge into the fabric, and the knot morphs without consistent topology.

The rock mostly stays still while the camera pushes in, but its painted pattern changes between frames and it seems to slide forward without turning. No rolling up or down actually happens, and the sand mound in front of it shifts oddly.

The bull and rider shapes keep morphing and don't hold together. The bull's body changes form and orientation between frames, the rider seems to merge with it, and the grab pole stays fixed in frame while everything around it swirls in ways that don't add up to a coherent spinning motion.

A pre-formed bow tie lies on a table while hands pinch and adjust its wings and strap. No real tying happens, but the fabric deforms only slightly and the hand contact looks plausible. There are minor shape shifts in the bow between frames, with no clear impossible event.

The Segway keeps changing shape and color between frames, ending up as a red boxy body, and its wheels and orientation shift inconsistently. The background pedestrians also change abruptly, so the vehicle's identity and motion are not continuous.

The ball floats around the person at roughly head height for long stretches without clearly being struck. At 5.12 s it hovers in mid-air beside her torso while her hands are down, and her arms and pose change in ways that don't match any contact with the ball. This looks like the ball hanging or drifting rather than following ballistic arcs.

The near golf ball beside the golfer disappears between 0 and 0.88 s without being shown moving, and nothing visibly rolls across the green. The distant ball stays fixed in place. The club swings, but the ball's sudden vanishing and the lack of any rolling motion are implausible.
Mostly static close-up of a dart embedded near the bullseye. The dart stays fixed with slight camera drift, and no implausible motion is visible.

The baseball lingers beside the wall for seconds, moving slowly while an enormous dust cloud billows out of a brick wall far beyond what a baseball impact would produce. The ball then fades or morphs inside the cloud, and no clear impact or mark is ever shown.

A skater glides toward the camera with small strides and leans into a speed-skating crouch. The motion and body posture look plausible, with no clear object or body violations, though the skating mechanics are a bit stiff and there is no actual wall push.

A close-up low-angle shot of a ball being dribbled near the feet. The ball's position jumps around between frames, sometimes left and sometimes right. At one point a hand reaches toward a ball it isn't actually touching, and the ball seems to move without a clear bounce trajectory. Then it floats near the player's knee and thigh, as if it is being juggled, with no clear impact, which looks inconsistent with a kick and rebound.

A boy holds a disc in his hand, then swings his arm forward in a throwing motion; the disc stays in his hand and tilts as it is released. The motion looks natural, with no impossible movement, though the disc hasn't visibly left his hand yet.

The dart on the board stays fixed at the same spot through the first frames, then a dart is seen floating in mid-air at 3.19 s, away from the board, with no thrower's arm in motion. By 3.75 s the board's dart has vanished. The player's hand movements are inconsistent, with darts appearing and disappearing in the hand, and the dart that was stuck in the board disappears without being pulled out.

The painted rock stays at roughly the same screen position on the slope while the dune and trail marks shift, and its colors and pattern change from frame to frame (green/yellow to solid blue to green/blue), which a real rock would not do. The depressions in the sand look like footprints rather than a rolling trail, and the rock leaves no continuous groove. The rock's apparent motion does not match a clear roll up or down.

An athlete runs across soft sand toward the camera; the shadow, stride and sand kicked up behind the feet look consistent, and the footprints and indentations are plausible. The sparse frames show no obvious glitches such as floating, sliding or inconsistent shadows.

A boxer in silhouette repeatedly punches a hanging heavy bag, which swings away from each hit and back on its chains in a believable way. The swing amplitude and timing match the punches, and I saw no clipping, floating or other physics errors.

The boy holds the ball, then it appears to drop and he dribbles it with his hand; the ball's position, motion blur and bounce spacing look like a normal dribble. It isn't an underhand throw, but that is a prompt mismatch, not a physics problem. At 1.06 s the ball is slightly detached in front of his hand, which is plausible for a release. No clear violations.

A man grabs the toolbox by its handle and lifts and tilts it, then it vanishes from view as the camera swings away. The final frames show an empty floor with no toolbox, no impact and no visible fall. The toolbox seems to disappear, and the scene shifts abruptly, so the fall is never shown. The toolbox also changes shape and size between frames.

The kite stays aloft with a taut string and tail trailing naturally while the camera pans and the kite drifts toward the tree. It never really descends or catches in the branches, which is a prompt mismatch but not a physics violation. Nothing moves in an impossible way, though the kite's rotation relative to the tree is slightly odd.

The hose repeatedly morphs between a smooth tube with a small kink and a long spiral-ribbed, flat, corkscrew shape. Its geometry changes without any cause, the end cap flips orientation, and the hose floats unsupported in the air. A real hose would not change form like this, so the physics is clearly broken.

Close-up of hands knitting cream yarn on metal needles; the motions repeat in a consistent cycle, the fabric stays attached to the needles, and the yarn and stitches look consistent between frames. No obvious interpenetration or impossible deformation is visible.

A stylist holds two hair dryers over a seated client's hair, and the hair stays smooth with the parting visible throughout; the dryer nozzles, hands and apron positions shift plausibly between samples and faint steam/air effects look consistent with hot airflow. No objects appear or vanish unnaturally, so physics looks largely plausible, with only minor ambiguity in the dryer positions.

The frames show a player holding and then throwing a football underhand, with the ball moving plausibly through the air. However, the later frames show the player crouched with the ball in hand and the ball disappearing or merging with the body, and the figure's shape and limbs look distorted in the final frames, suggesting morphing or inconsistent object continuity; the ball's trajectory and landing are not clearly visible.

The frames show a crane claw and a container lid with the claw moving slightly and not visibly contacting or shifting the container; the container stays in place across frames, so nothing visibly violates physics, though the claw's motion between frames is somewhat jerky and the promised nudge is not clearly shown.

The frisbee lies on the grass from the start and slides/tumbles across the ground, shifting position and orientation between frames (it appears to slide and rotate slightly, sometimes showing its edge) before coming to rest. The sliding and gradual deceleration on grass are plausible, though the frisbee seems to move without a clear throw and its rotation/position changes are a bit inconsistent between frames.

The hood starts propped open with a stick held by a hand, then the stick slips and the hood progressively drops toward the closed position, with the hood moving smoothly and gravity-consistent across frames. The motion of the hood lowering is plausible, though the stick and hand motion in the early frames is somewhat ambiguous.

The peeler sits in a hand and removes thin strips of potato skin that curl away from the tuber, which is plausible. Frames show the potato staying stable while the peeler moves, and the strip stays attached and curls naturally. The only oddity is the potato apparently not rotating, but the physics of peeling is broadly consistent.

A horseshoe spins through the air in a tumbling arc, appearing at varying orientations across frames consistent with rotation, and the sequence of frames shows it rising and falling; the gap between frames is plausible for a tossed horseshoe. No obvious violation of gravity, rotation, or momentum is visible, though the exact landing around the stake is not shown in the sampled frames.

The frames show a tightrope walker standing and balancing on the line with bare feet, moving normally with no visible fall or harness catch. The prompt describes a fall and harness catch, which never appears in these sampled frames; the walker stays on the rope throughout, with plausible body posture and a rope that does not visibly deform unrealistically.

A person's hands handle a dark leather shoe and black lace in a plausible manner; the lace ends move and loop in ways consistent with being pulled and manipulated by hands, with no objects appearing or vanishing unnaturally. A second arm/hand appearing at the top edge in some frames is consistent with a helper or the person's other hand, and the shoe stays stable on the leg.

The frames show a barbell with plates in a weightlifting snatch from multiple blurred camera angles; the bar moves continuously and the plates stay attached to the bar ends across frames, with no obvious object appearing, vanishing, or teleporting. Motion blur and lighting shifts are consistent with camera movement, though the bar's orientation changes between angles are somewhat hard to track.

Two people hold opposite ends of a bungee cord and stretch it; the cord's length changes plausibly between frames with hands moving apart and together, though the cord's apparent length and shape shift somewhat abruptly and the hand positions and arm overlaps look a bit inconsistent across frames (e.g., a second arm appears and disappears near the red-shirt person). Overall the motion is mostly plausible with minor continuity oddities.

The ball appears in hand at 0.00 s, then a blurry ball is seen near the tree at 0.71 s, but the thrower's glove is later pressed against the brick wall with no visible ball impact or rebound trajectory, and the ball is never seen bouncing off the wall. The ball's path and the throw-and-rebound sequence are not coherent, with the ball seemingly vanishing and the player's arm posture changing without a clear throw.

Kibble pours from an inverted bag into a bowl with a steady stream that piles up in the bowl and settles plausibly under gravity, with pieces tumbling and bouncing onto the heap. The pile level rises gradually across frames, consistent with continuous pouring; no objects appear or vanish unnaturally.

The frames show only a static snowy scene with a fence and falling snow flakes; no snowball is visibly thrown or hits the fence, and no wet indentation appears. Nothing visibly violates physics, though the expected action is absent, and the falling flakes and lighting remain consistent across frames.

A hammer head enters from above and impacts the concrete block edge; concrete chunks then fly off and scatter with plausible momentum and fragmentation, with debris falling and dispersing. The block appears to remain in place while fragments break away from the impact point, which is consistent with real impact behavior, though the hammer's contact and the rapid debris ejection are slightly stylized.

The painted rock appears to roll toward the camera, leaving a sand trail, but across frames it moves and its position shifts plausibly while the trail and sand texture remain consistent. Its shadow and orientation shift in a way that roughly fits rolling, though the rock seems to grow larger and closer as it moves and the trail behind it is not clearly consistent with a rock rolling back down an incline.

The frames show two people tying a black sneaker's laces with hands moving in a plausible sequence; laces loop, cross and pull through without visible impossible deformation or floating. Shoe and hands stay consistent between samples, with only minor ambiguity in lace routing that could be hidden between frames.

The balloon appears already inflated in all frames without visible air filling, which is a sparse-sampling gap but not clearly impossible. The toy is held near the neck and inserted through the opening, with the balloon remaining taut and the toy appearing to sit inside the balloon, which is plausible; the ribbon and tying hand are also consistent with a real action. Some hand/ribbon shapes look slightly soft, but no clear violation of object motion or gravity is visible.

The gymnast stands on the beam, raises and spreads her arms, then bends forward and rotates over the beam in a forward roll; the body's motion and rotation look plausible, though the frames show her hands and body inverted over the beam with the hair flying, and the transition to lying across the beam at 6.00 s is somewhat abrupt but roughly consistent with a roll that stays on the beam. The motion is mostly continuous with no objects appearing or vanishing, so only minor doubts about the exact contact between body and beam arise.

The towel starts draped over the chair back and transitions to a rolled, then flat folded state on the seat, which is a physically odd sequence: a towel would not spontaneously roll itself up and then flatten into a neat rectangle without any visible hand or force. The motion between frames is abrupt and the fabric changes shape implausibly fast.

The ball bounces off the wooden court with plausible motion: it rises and falls, and hands and legs contact it at reasonable points. Frame-to-frame changes in the ball's position and the hand placement are consistent with a gentle dribble, though some blur and shape distortion make exact contact hard to verify. No obvious floating, teleporting, or impossible deformation is visible.

The paddle blade appears planted in the mud/bank while the person leans into it, but the camera angle shifts and the person and scenery move in ways that suggest the view changes rather than the kayak being pushed up the bank; the kayak itself is never visible, and the paddle seems to pass through or rest on the ground without clear mud displacement or resistance. Overall the motion is mostly plausible but the interaction with the mud and kayak is ambiguous and the paddle's position shifts somewhat oddly between frames.

The hammer stays essentially in the same place on the floor across all frames, with no visible throw, bounce, or motion, and the wall shows no new mark. The prompt describes a forceful throw and bounce, which would require clear motion and an impact, so the frames show physics-violating stillness (an object that should be moving or falling is static), though a static scene itself is not a physics error.

The table surface and napkin move plausibly: a hand folds the fabric, and the napkin rests on the table with soft, believable drape and no objects appearing, vanishing, or floating. The napkin ring is not visible, so the prompt's ring placement is not shown, but nothing violates physics between frames.

The ball flies toward the brick wall, strikes it with a burst of dust and brick debris, and then appears to rebound and tumble away from the wall, while dust clouds spread and settle. The ball and debris motion look broadly plausible, though the rebound direction and the ball seeming to travel back through the dust cloud are somewhat ambiguous and slightly unusual for a hard impact.

The water blob floats in mid-air with no visible hand, holder, or support, and its shape shifts between frames and surface texture changes, which is not how a water balloon behaves; it looks like a floating liquid mass that never stretches a rubber skin as the prompt describes. Physics of the liquid's suspension and deformation is implausible.

The pot is shown on a shelf/counter, then at 2.12 s it appears to float in mid-air above the counter edge with no visible support, then it tilts and lands with debris scattering, which is plausible. However the pot seems to hover before falling and the pot's position shifts oddly, and the fragments and debris appear to spread without clear impact, so there are some physics irregularities.

The blue-suited surfer's body and board appear to change abruptly between frames: the board and person shift scale and position discontinuously, the red surfer teleports closer and merges with the blue surfer, and the blue surfer's limbs and wetsuit look distorted during the collision. The fall and swim-away motion are not smoothly continuous, so the physics of the collision breaks down.

The player runs, then the ball appears in the air beside her at 2.12 s and is repeatedly struck and kept aloft over several frames; the ball's position and size change plausibly and it stays in the air while she moves, with no obvious impossible motion. Some ball-to-foot contact is not clearly shown, but the sequence is broadly consistent with a kick and arc, with only minor ambiguity about how the ball gets airborne.

The hammer strikes the block and the block cracks and fragments with plausible debris and dust, but the block seems to be a brick-like object with inconsistent geometry: the hollow interior and the fragments appear to morph between frames, and the hammer head shifts position oddly with a stray fragment flying. Overall the impact-and-break sequence is mostly plausible with some visual inconsistencies in how the broken pieces reassemble and settle.

The frames show a pole vaulter running and then the body swinging with the pole in the background, but the pole itself is not clearly visible bending; the athlete's limbs and body appear to shift oddly between frames, with the figure seeming to lean in an unsupported way and the pole/box interaction not clearly depicted. Overall the motion is plausible for a vault approach but the transitions between frames are somewhat ambiguous.

The pole and athlete appear inconsistently: the vaulter seems to float in mid-air with the pole changing position and angle abruptly between frames, and the athlete's body orientation and grip on the pole look unnatural, with the pole apparently bending/rotating without a clear plant or run-up. The jump lacks a convincing run-up and takeoff, and the athlete's trajectory and pole interaction do not follow a coherent real-world pole vault motion.

The athlete runs across grass, then on the track, and the frames show a body rotating and flailing in midair with the body becoming horizontal and then diving face-first onto the track, which is plausible for a long jump or dive. However, the body position changes abruptly between frames (rapid rotation, limbs and head warping, a divot-like mark appearing on the track before landing) and the grass-to-track transition is inconsistent with the runner's path, so some motion looks unnatural.

The yo-yo appears to be pressed flat or into the wall and deforms in a way that looks like it sinks into or merges with the brick surface, with no clear rebound trajectory away from the wall; it also seems to be stuck or hovering against the wall rather than bouncing back with a plausible arc. The yo-yo's string also behaves oddly, hanging from above while the body is pinned against the wall, so the motion and contact look physically implausible.

The sequence starts with the jumper already in the sand pit at 0.00 s, then shows him landing at 0.88 s, but the later frames show him running down the runway and leaping in the air well after the landing, so the order of events is reversed relative to the prompt's long jump. Frame 0.88 s shows a hand planted on the runway edge while his body is in the sand, and the later frames show him in a flight-like pose on the runway, which is inconsistent with a continuous jump arc. The camera and runway geometry are plausible, but the timeline of takeoff, flight and landing does not follow normal physics.

The ball moves from the player's hands upward and then over the net in a plausible arc, with the player's arms and body following a consistent swing motion. Ball size, lighting and motion blur are consistent across frames, and nothing appears to teleport or defy gravity, though the ball's exact contact and trajectory are hard to verify from sparse frames.

A stick enters the mud wall at 0.00 s and a small dark hole appears in the surface; afterward the stick disappears from view and the hole stays static, with no falling debris or inconsistent deformation. The sequence is plausible for a stick poking into a soft mud surface, though the stick seems to vanish quickly, which is a minor oddity.

The player is on ice in skates with a hockey stick, which is plausible for ice hockey, though the prompt describes a field-hockey style drag flick from the ground. The frames show a stick and a puck-like object on the ice; the player's skates and body movements look consistent with skating and a shot, with no obvious objects appearing or vanishing or floating unnaturally. A ball/puck appears near the player at 3.38 s and later a puck sits on the ice, which is plausible; the motion is continuous and gravity-consistent overall.

The woman handles a red fabric tie with hands and fingers that stay coherent across frames; the fabric drapes, folds and hangs as cloth would, and the knot forms gradually as she manipulates the loose end. Sparse sampling leaves some gaps in how the wrapping and threading happen, but nothing clearly defies physics such as floating or passing through the body.

The skaters move on wheels across the floor with plausible motion, leaning and spinning; however the blue-clad skater appears to float or hop with skates lifted off the floor in several frames (e.g., 2.62 s, 3.38 s) and the two skaters seem to pass through or merge with each other around 4.25 s, which are noticeable physics oddities.

The golfer's stance and swing are plausible, but the later close-up frames show the ball hovering in mid-air above the green for about two seconds, drifting only slightly, with no visible arc or landing. A ball that should be rolling along the turf instead appears to float, which breaks basic motion physics.

The prompt asks for a pancake stack to tip over and fall, but across the sampled frames the stack stays perfectly upright on the plate with no tilting, shifting, or falling; the syrup and a stray droplet move slightly but the stack itself is static. This fails to show the described toppling, which is a physics-inconsistent outcome for a stack that should fall under gravity once it tips.

The ball sits on the floor, bounces up and down in a plausible arc with a slight squash on contact, and rises and falls smoothly between frames. The ball's size and position relative to the court lines and net stay consistent, with no abrupt jumps or unexplained motion. Shadows and lighting remain coherent, though the bounce looks slightly floaty and the ball's apparent height varies a bit with perspective.

The child holds a small dart at arm's length and it stays in the hand/tip region across frames, with no visible throwing motion; the dart appears to shift position gradually and drift toward the board while the arm extends and retracts slowly, rather than being released and flying. The dart seems to hover or move with the hand, which is not how a thrown dart travels, though the sampled frames are sparse and the throw itself is not clearly shown.

The child holds a dart at 0-1.4 s, then the scene cuts to a different dartboard with darts stuck in the board's edge area and the child throwing. Darts fly toward the board and one dart appears to float or drift at 3.58 s, and a dart falls to the floor at 4.29 s, which is plausible for a miss, but the object trajectories and hand-held darts look inconsistent between frames, with a dart seeming to hang in mid-air.

The frames show a close-up of a yellow machine's rear with a chain hanging down and dragging on the ground; the chain stays taut-looking and the machine appears to move forward while dust rises, which is plausible. The chain's lower end seems to stay near the ground, and the scene becomes obscured by dust later, with no obvious object-permanence or fluid/rigid-body violations visible.

The rider on the unicycle-like wheel is seen riding smoothly along a curving path, then at 0.71 s to 1.42 s the frames show the body leaning and a foot coming down near the wheel, which is plausible for stopping. After that the frames zoom in and the rider stays stationary with hands on the handlebar while the background stays unchanged, which is consistent with a brief stop, though the bike's body shape and foot placement shift somewhat between close-ups.

The stack of blue papers stays mostly intact and only a few top sheets lift, flutter and drift in the air before settling back, which is roughly consistent with a gust acting on light paper. However, the sheets appear to rise and hover in a somewhat unnatural way and the stack's overall shape shifts oddly between frames, so the motion is only partly plausible.

The squash court and players' movements look mostly natural: the red-shirted player moves across the court, the blue-shirted player swings and recovers, and the camera pans. Some frames show abrupt changes in racket position and player placement between samples, and the blue player's racket and body appear to jump somewhat, but these could be sampling gaps or motion blur rather than clear violations of gravity, momentum, or contact.

A worker drags a scoring tool along the surface of a thick light-colored slab across frames, with the tile appearing intact throughout and no visible crack, break, or fragment separation. The tool and hand motions look plausible, and the slab stays rigid and in place, so nothing obviously violates physics, though the lack of a fracture by the end is a mild mismatch with the prompt rather than a physics error.

The hula hoops show motion blur and overlapping rings consistent with fast spinning, and the hoops appear to stay in plausible positions around the waists of the two people across frames. Some hoop shapes look deformed or merged between frames, which is a minor visual oddity, but the overall motion reads as physically normal.

The frames show a player throwing darts at a board mounted on a wall; darts appear stuck in the board and the player walks up to retrieve them between throws. One oddity: at 4.25 s the dart cluster near the bull and the dart positions shift plausibly, and at 6.00 s a dart appears in the bull area, which is consistent with throws, though the player seems to handle darts at the board rather than visibly throwing each one. Overall motion and dart landings look largely plausible.

A dark ball appears at the left-center and then rolls toward the camera, and a light ball enters from the right at 4.25 s, which could plausibly be the struck cue ball hitting it; a dark ball then appears at 5.12 s and rolls away to the left, with the other ball leaving frame. The sparse frames make the collision hard to verify, and there is a minor oddity in ball identity and positions, but the motion looks largely consistent with rolling balls on felt.

The yo-yo appears to be thrown toward the brick wall and then returns on its string, with the frames showing it spinning and swinging back plausibly. The motion blur and the string hanging from the top suggest a yo-yo on a string bouncing off the wall without visible damage, consistent with the prompt. Some rotation and position changes between sparse frames are hard to fully verify, but nothing clearly violates physics.

The worker holds a small framed picture against a frosted glass panel with a suction cup and the picture stays attached through the frames; the picture appears to be a stuck-on object on the glass, and the worker's hand/tool movements look plausible, with no obvious floating or sudden disappearance. The picture stays affixed as the prompt describes, but the suction-cup lifting of a heavy panel is not clearly shown, and the picture's sticking to glass is at least plausible in a close-up frame sequence.

The person runs, then jumps and the skateboard appears beneath/ahead of him mid-air, with the board flipping and drifting apart from his feet in a way that doesn't match a board being kicked or landed on; in later frames the board hovers and spins at a distance from him with no visible contact, and the backflip is ambiguous, so the object motion and contact physics look implausible.

The Segway-like vehicle is initially ridden by a person in the middle of the crowd, then a rider appears on it while the vehicle moves steadily and turns, and the rider is seated consistently. However, the vehicle's position and the rider's identity change abruptly between frames (a blurred figure, then a different man with a seat), and the vehicle seems to swap between seated and standing configurations and wheel placements, with the final frame showing the vehicle and rider apparently moving off-frame at an odd scale, suggesting noticeable discontinuities in motion and object persistence.

The frames show a red tie being looped and tightened into a knot around the neck, with the loose end hanging down. The tie's fabric folds, drapes, and tightens in a manner consistent with real silk or satin, and the hand manipulations are plausible; there are no obvious discontinuities, floating objects, or impossible deformations, though the knot's exact structure shifts somewhat between frames as expected from hand movements.

The frames show a thin pastry sheet draped over a stack of layered phyllo dough, with the top sheet shifting and lifting in a way consistent with soft dough being handled and draped under gravity. The layers appear to stay coherent with no implausible teleporting, melting, or floating, though the sheet's motion between frames is somewhat hard to track precisely.

A rider in a red jacket pedals a fat-tire mountain bike up a snowy slope, leaving tracks in the deep snow consistent with the prompt. The bike, rider, and snow interaction look plausible across frames, with the rider's position progressing smoothly up the hill and the background skier moving consistently.

The dart appears already embedded in the wire at the center across all frames, which is plausible for a landed dart; the dart stays static with no visible motion of the flight or impact. At 2.62 s a dart tail appears at the left edge, which may be a second dart or the player's hand, but the embedded dart does not move unrealistically, so physics looks mostly consistent.

The climber in a helmet and harness holds a rope and moves along a mossy rock face in a plausible manner; the rope, carabiner and body positions stay consistent across frames with no objects floating, teleporting, or unnatural limb motion. Movement is slow and controlled as expected for a rope descent.

The first two frames show a sheet being torn by two gloved hands with a plausible jagged tear. Later frames show a different scene: the paper appears to be fed or sliding over a printer-like surface with a hand holding one edge, and the sheet's shape and position change abruptly between samples, with the paper seemingly reappearing as a whole piece rather than two halves, which is physically inconsistent.

The balloon appears to pop into fragments at around 0.7-1.4 s, but the frames show the red balloon intact and floating near the fence afterward, with the dog and balloon moving in plausible ways. The sudden appearance of a large red balloon/fragment cloud and the balloon reappearing whole after a burst is inconsistent, and the balloon seems to change size and position abruptly between frames.

The two balloons start as one stacked, with the upper one shifting and then the lower one bulging. The lower balloon bursts with shards flying outward, but the fragments then collapse into a heap of wrinkled, gel-like red material that looks like a melted or solidified mass rather than a rubber balloon deflating, and the pieces appear to lose their structure and volume in an implausible way. This is a noticeable departure from how a burst latex balloon should look and move.

A woman stuffs a white pillowcase into a red laundry bag; the fabric drapes, folds and bulges plausibly as it is pushed in, and the camera perspective is consistent. Some frames are blurry and the bag's rim shape shifts somewhat, but the cloth motion and hand interactions look broadly physically reasonable.

The parasail stays roughly in the same relative position above and behind the boat across frames, with the boat moving steadily and leaving a consistent wake on calm water. The canopy stays inflated and the motion is smooth, so nothing obvious breaks physics; only the subtle drift of the canopy and boat position across the frames is worth noting.

The first frames show a flat-lying black tool case on a sloped bench with its handle hanging off the edge, which is plausible given its weight and shape. Later, a man sets a second, smaller case on top of the flat case and it rests stably with its weight supported, which is also plausible. The camera angle shifts between frames, but nothing obviously defies gravity or contact physics.

The frames show players moving on a court with plausible footwork and body motion, and a white ball appears on the ground near a player at 6.00 s, which could be a shuttlecock or ball that has landed; the sparse frames do not clearly show an impossible event, though the ball appearing with a racket and no visible clear shot is somewhat ambiguous and the object looks more like a tennis ball than a shuttlecock.

The frames show a gloved hand holding a rotary cutter over layered colorful fabric, with the blade moving along the fabric and the cloth staying flat on the table. The tool's position shifts between frames in a plausible way, though the cutter's blade orientation and hand pose change somewhat abruptly around 1.42 s, a minor visual inconsistency rather than a clear physics violation.

The athlete jumps and extends legs, then the camera moves close as the body appears to rise and arms spread; the frames show plausible human motion, with the figure seemingly airborne early and then the camera framing shifts to close-ups. Only sparse samples exist, and the scale/camera changes are plausible for a slow-motion shot, so no clear physics violation is visible.

The two red boats move across calm water with consistent wakes and spray, and the towing relationship looks plausible; the lead boat's position and scale shift somewhat between frames (it appears to grow closer to the camera and its shape changes), suggesting some morphing or camera-perspective inconsistency, but no clear gross violation of water, buoyancy, or motion physics is evident.

The frames show a static bowling lane with pins standing in their set positions and no ball, pinsetter, or people moving; the camera appears to shift slightly in framing and lighting varies a bit, but nothing physically implausible occurs between samples.

The frames show a person juggling a ball with feet and head; the ball positions and motion look broadly plausible, with arcs and contacts consistent with kicks and headers. Some frames are blurry and the ball's appearance shifts somewhat between frames, but the sparse samples don't show clear violations of gravity, contact, or momentum.

The climber's gloved hand holds the ice tool/screw in the ice across frames, with the body and arm moving smoothly and no objects appearing, vanishing, or floating unnaturally. The screw appears to shift slightly outward over time, which is plausible for a screw being withdrawn, and the ice and background remain consistent.

The climber's body position, harness, rope and belay device stay consistent across frames, and the camera angle shifts smoothly, but the climber appears to move up the rock face and reposition his hands and feet (frames 2-4 show him climbing higher with arms reaching up) rather than steadily descending on the rope as the prompt describes. The rope also shows no clear lowering motion, so the apparent upward movement conflicts with the gravity-driven descent expected.

The stack of dominoes is nudged at the top and then appears to shatter into many fragments and scatter across the surface, with pieces flying and bouncing in all directions rather than toppling in sequence as rigid dominoes would. The dominoes break apart and seem to fly outward unnaturally, and a piece appears to vanish or drift off-frame, which is not how rigid blocks would fall.

A seated person handles a shoelace and shoe with hands and what looks like a lace-tying aid; the lace, hands and shoe move in a plausible way across frames, with no objects appearing, vanishing or passing through each other. Some hand and lace shapes are a bit fluid, but nothing clearly defies physics.

The person juggles a soccer ball that rises and falls in plausible arcs, with the ball's apparent size and position changing consistently across frames. The ball appears at the top edge at 0.00 s and at 6.00 s, consistent with a juggling cycle, and no objects pass through bodies or float unnaturally.

The person wades through muddy puddles with boots sinking and mud clinging plausibly to the boots and gloves; footprints and splashing are consistent. Later frames show the person standing and turning in a wide muddy field, with the camera framing shifting to show a hat-wearing figure, which is plausible continuity without obvious physical violations.

The bow tie stays a rigid, consistent shape and the hands manipulate the fabric plausibly; the long tail of the tie shifts between frames as it would when being pulled through a loop. The jumps between sparse samples are consistent with a time-lapse edit, and nothing clearly defies gravity, rigidity, or material behavior.

The pumpkin sits on the stool for the first several seconds with no visible change, then at 6.00 s the stool appears to be collapsing and the pumpkin is squashed/deformed and sinking low, looking more like a soft-body glitch than a rigid pumpkin rolling off. The stool's legs are splayed and the pumpkin's shape distorts unnaturally during the transition, with the intermediate fall and roll not visibly shown between samples.

The camera glides along a wooden closet while stacks of folded white linens and beige towels stay upright and stable on the shelves, which is plausible. Some stacks and shelf contents shift in count and position between samples, which may be camera perspective or small inconsistencies rather than clear physics violations.

The snowmobile moves smoothly across the frozen lake with a consistent snow spray trailing behind it, and the camera drifts with it. The rider stays upright and the machine keeps plausible contact with the snow; the snowmobile's position shifts gradually between frames, and the tree and shoreline geometry stays consistent, with no obvious physical impossibility.

The toothpaste squeezed from the tube forms a dripping, cohesive string that falls under gravity onto the toothbrush bristles, with blobs forming and detaching naturally. The stream intermittently breaks and rejoins as the squeeze varies, which is plausible for a viscous paste; the brush stays in place and the paste lands on it. Minor oddities such as the stream appearing to thin or run in sheets at 1.75 s are within normal viscous-fluid behavior.

The red paper-cut streamer sways and twists as a flexible sheet, with plausible bending and fluttering motion against a consistent landscape background. The swimmer's body is anatomically incoherent. Early frames show a long elongated torso-limb with no clear head, and later frames show an arm emerging from the middle of the back at odd angles, so the body morphs unnaturally from frame to frame. The splashing water looks fairly plausible.

The rest of the scene stays fixed, so this looks like the object moving rather than the camera panning. No real poke happens, and the feather's steady drift away doesn't match a slight shift from a touch.

A hand holds a wrench near the wheel, but the wrench never engages a bolt; it floats in front of the tire and is then gone along with the hand. Objects also show up on the ground out of nowhere, and the wheel never comes off. The tool interaction is implausible.
