The tires leave no visible tracks, and the bike's geometry shifts oddly between frames. In the later frames the rider seems to glide with little interaction with the deep snow, which looks somewhat implausible.

The climber stands at the base of the wall handling a green rope and then places a hand on the rock. The rope seems to tangle and loop oddly near her hands, and the rope's attachment point is ambiguous. Her body motion and contact with the wall look mostly natural, with only minor rope inconsistencies.

A huge water splash appears in front of the camera with no balloon bursting. Afterward an intact yellow balloon floats, rises and stays near the man, and the splashes keep reappearing around his feet. The sequence looks like reversed or incoherent motion, with water and balloon behaving implausibly.

A large multicolored canopy, like a parachute or balloon envelope, billows and deforms in the wind against the sky, with plausible fabric dynamics and lines visible. The panel patterns shift a little oddly, but no clear physical violation shows.

A hand rests its fingertips on a disc on top of a stack of CD cases, then leaves, and the stack stays still. Nothing physically implausible happens: no penetration, the objects don't deform oddly, and the rest state stays stable. The only odd point is that the hand disappears quickly between frames.

The person crouches in the mud next to the kayak. The kayak keeps changing size and orientation, growing longer and turning from end-on to side-on, without any visible push that would cause it, and the person's body seems to merge with the kayak. No paddle is shown, and the kayak's motion is inconsistent with the forces being applied.

The thread wrapped around the needle eye changes and vanishes between frames, and the needle stands upright with nothing holding it after the fingers let go. A second needle then passes through the eye and the thread appears and disappears without a cause, so objects and thread are inconsistent from frame to frame.

Beer pours steadily from the tilted bottle into the mug. The foam head grows and the liquid level rises gradually, and the bottle tilts more as it empties, all consistent with real pouring. The beer level inside the bottle looks a bit odd, but nothing clearly breaks physics.

The toothbrush appears to be held by nothing, floating in mid-air near the faucet, and the toothpaste shows up on the brush oddly: it is blue-white and appears on the bristles without a clear continuous stream from the nozzle. The bristles also change. The tube's deformation does not match the squeezing well either.

A welder moves a torch along a car frame. The sparks start out heavy and then mostly disappear, and the flame changes from orange to a blue torch flame. The torch also seems to partly enter or merge with the panel opening, and there is no weld bead or visible progress. These are minor inconsistencies, but the overall motion is plausible.

Between 0 and 0.75 s the green ball turns into a blue ball. The red ball on the left and the cream ball on the right vanish without any visible pocketing or plausible motion, and an orange ball later appears from nowhere. Objects changing identity and appearing or disappearing breaks object permanence.

The skater's body morphs throughout. Limbs and legs change configuration in ways that don't follow continuous motion, the head becomes a featureless red blob, and the skater appears to hang mid-air in odd poses without a clear jump. The skates also seem to glide or slide without any push-off from a wall.

The ice sphere changes shape on its own, going from a perfect sphere to lumpy and dented and then roundish again, without the tool ever clearly touching it. The internal features also appear and vanish. There is no carving debris or water, and the tool bit floats near the ice rather than cutting it.

A climber handles carabiners and ropes against a rock face. The motion is mostly smooth and plausible, though the gear and hands shift and merge a little, and the gear seems to rearrange without clear manipulation.

The knife never spins or flies. It sits almost still in the cork, slowly sinking, while dark burn-like marks spread and grow outward on their own with no cause. The blade also changes shape and width over time.

The spindle stays still with its yarn intact while a hand pulls a strand. The yarn connection is inconsistent: the strand appears from nowhere, and the hand reaches behind the wheel. These are minor oddities, and the scene shows no clear physical violation.

The skater rides the board steadily the whole time, but the board moves along while the rider's foot placement and body orientation shift oddly. In the last frame the person is suddenly floating well above and behind the board, which keeps rolling on alone, with no clear jump motion. Body proportions also morph between frames (the hair appears and the build changes).

A small leaf pile grows into an enormous dome-shaped mass that rises up and fills the whole frame, far larger than the amount of leaves at the start. The leaves hold a solid mound shape instead of scattering along the street with the wind, so leaf volume is not conserved and the motion is not plausible.

The jumper swings on the cord, but body orientation changes oddly: it flips from inverted to upright, then stays nearly horizontal and perpendicular to a taut cord near the end, which doesn't fit how a body hangs under tension. The figure's shape also morphs between frames.

The frisbee appears out of nowhere at the child's hip around 1.73 s, with no flight toward the child, and then shows up already held at arm's length. The child's appearance also shifts between frames, so the catch is never physically shown.

The bottle cap changes form across the frames: it is a solid crown cap at first, but later the bottle top shows an open mouth with a ring-like cap still around it. The pliers grip the cap but it ends up looking open without ever being pried off, and the cap shows no believable bending.

No toy car is visible for the first ~3 seconds, then one appears in the child's hand from nowhere. The car never rolls down the ramp; it sits at the bottom or moves on the floor while being held, and the ramp seems to merge with the blocks.

The nunchucks are never coherent: they morph into wooden blocks held in the hands, and the pile of blocks grows and reshapes without any real impacts. Debris floats around oddly, and the person's hands seem to pass through objects.

The group of players in the foreground merges into a tangled heap of bodies at 2–2.9 s and then vanishes completely by 3.58 s. New players appear lined up at the left with no visible movement to get there.

The right swimmer's body deforms impossibly. Her head and upper torso disappear, leaving a headless torso with arms sprouting from odd places, and then she reforms facing a different direction. Her legs also morph between poses.

Hands adjust a wire sculpture that stands on a coiled base, then the hands let go. The sculpture stays upright and keeps its shape. The wire morphs a little between frames, but nothing grossly implausible happens; the top-heavy figure balancing on a coil is plausible for a stiff wire.

The candle flame stays lit and steady the whole time, yet thick, wispy smoke streams rise as if it had just been blown out. A calm, burning flame wouldn't produce that much smoke, and no puff of air visibly disturbs the flame.

The hands hover near the knot and appear to fiddle with it, but the tie never actually loosens or changes. The fingers seem to pass over or into the fabric without any real grip or deformation, so the cloth doesn't respond to how it is being handled. The motion is ambiguous, though, and could pass as adjusting the tie.

The bike moves through deep snow yet leaves almost no clear tracks or ruts behind it, and the wheels sit on or above the snow instead of sinking in. The bike geometry also changes between frames, and the rider's foot and pedals don't move in a consistent pedaling motion.
Plates stacked on a turntable spin with motion blur while the camera slowly tilts and moves up. The stacked plates stay seated, and there is no clear deformation or object inconsistency.

The bottle seems to change form across frames. A large labelled green bottle turns into a blurry object, and the last frame shows a different-looking bottle neck with a wire bail clamp that seems attached oddly to a second glass piece. The opening action is not coherent: the label and bottle disappear and the clamp geometry is implausible.

The pumpkin lifts off the stool and floats in mid-air, rotating, for several seconds with no support, then settles back onto the stool. The stool never breaks, and debris appears on the seat. Levitating against gravity is a clear physics violation.

The post changes shape and material between frames, from a square wooden stake to a round pipe, and its height shifts. The tool also morphs, merging with the post and partly disappearing, and the gloves change color from blue to white. Nothing is shown being dug or packed in a believable way.

The hole is already there from the first frame, and the stick just slides into the existing opening without breaking any mud, scattering debris or deforming the wall. The interaction looks plausible on its own, though the contact feels a bit off and the stick seems to pass into the dark opening without resistance.

A figure dances and spins on a fashion runway, and the body morphs implausibly between frames. The face and back swap orientation erratically, the hair or headpiece changes shape, and the limbs and clothing distort in ways a real body could not.

The cyclist rides steadily toward the camera on a packed snow track. Bike motion, posture and the scene stay consistent across frames, with no clear anomalies. There is only a slight lean and some ambiguity about pedaling.

The player starts out holding the ball well behind the arc, and the ball never travels in a visible arc. It vanishes from his hands and then shows up near the rim during what looks like a dunk, while the player seems to slide from far court to the basket. Players also morph (#12 becomes the shooter), and the ball goes in and out of existence.

The ball's surface pattern changes and smears, the ball floats beside the shoe without clear support, and a hand appears near the ball, which then passes behind the leg and vanishes. The ball is inconsistent and disappears.

The scissors keep 'cutting' the thread, but it never separates. The thread loop appears, disappears and reappears inconsistently, and the scissor blades change color and shape between frames (blue, then silver, then blue). The cutting action has no real effect on the thread.

The early frames show two hands gripping the same bar, but later only one arm is on the bar, with the torso beside it. The second arm seems to vanish or merge into the body, which is anatomically inconsistent. No clear slip and recovery is shown.

A hand repeatedly flicks the small propeller on the toy's shaft, and it spins with motion blur while the toy stays stable. The hand and propeller interact consistently and nothing passes through anything, so this looks like real footage.

The ball floats near the net for over a second without crossing it. A second player appears on the near side, and in one frame the ball is held in her left hand while her racket is in her right. Then the ball moves away from her without a visible stroke, so its path is inconsistent.

The wing lies flat on the sand, yet the person's lines run straight up into the sky to a second canopy that appears in the upper right later in the clip. The wing on the ground also shrinks and shifts on its own, so the lines and wing don't connect in a physically consistent way.

The 'bubble gum' bubble is really an iridescent soap bubble coming straight from his lips. It detaches and drifts, then disappears completely between 1.42 s and 2.12 s without any popping or remnant. His lips then show pink gum that appears out of nowhere.

A brass tip floats at a dangling tool with no clear role, and the pen tip glows while the carved grooves stay the same. The wood shows no burn marks, smoke or new lines, yet the deep grooves look like a burner can't make them.

The black bike the rider starts on becomes a white-and-red bike partway through, and the rider's appearance changes too. In the later frames the bike tips into an odd, contorted position with the rider hunched over it, so objects and the person lack consistent identity and plausible motion.

A hammer comes in from the right edge, morphs in shape (head and handle change form between frames), seems to hover or rise, then leaves frame upward and vanishes with no bounce or resting position. Its motion and shape are inconsistent with a thrown rigid object.

The football just sits on the grass the whole time while a player's feet walk past it. Nothing implausible happens: no throw is shown, but the static ball and the walking legs are physically consistent, apart from small shifts that look like camera motion.

The gymnast never really leaps. Instead she morphs between poses: her hair changes from an up-do to long loose hair, and her legs float in split positions with no clear support on the beam. At 2.96 s the extended foot hovers in the air while her body stays upright without visible momentum. These inconsistent, support-less body configurations suggest implausible physics.

A pipette tip slowly approaches a small green insect on a leaf, and the insect shifts slightly. Its shape morphs a bit between frames, but the motion is subtle and nothing clearly impossible happens. The leaf moves gently and the contact is plausible.

The frames show a close-up of legs bouncing on a trampoline. The feet go out of frame at times, and the legs and shoes seem to change shape and appear or disappear inconsistently: a single shoe is visible, legs merge, and the leg configuration shifts in odd ways. Still, nothing is clearly impossible given the sparse sampling.

The glove appears and vanishes between frames, and a ball suddenly materializes in his bare hand. At 5.17 s a second ball or glove-like object appears from nowhere while he is still holding the first ball, so objects are spawning and disappearing.

The man goes from standing to lying flat face-down, then twists up into a kneeling position in a way that doesn't follow real body motion. A gray mat and ropes appear out of nowhere under him, and the rope and his harness gear change inconsistently between frames.

The ball's motion is inconsistent. It floats around the legs, vanishes near the ground at 1.73 s, then reappears mid-air at leg height with no visible bounce. It changes size and appears to hover rather than following a clear spiked trajectory into the ground.

A red ball appears out of nowhere, then turns into a cube-shaped '50' block, shrinks into a small cap, and grows back into a block. The bumper colors and positions also change between frames. Objects that morph, materialize and resize like this break physical commonsense.
A hand rests on a snowball while the other hand comes into view. The snowball's surface marks fade and shift slightly with no clear cause, but the motion is minimal and mostly plausible.

The toy hammer keeps changing shape and size: it becomes a large barrel-like object floating beside the child, then shrinks to a small orange object in his hand, then reappears as a full hammer. No toy is hit and nothing falls.

Riders on Segways move around a plaza with mostly plausible motion, but there are some generative inconsistencies: background riders and pedestrians appear, shift, and merge between frames, and some figures in the group seem to change identity or pop in. The foreground riders' motion is mostly smooth.

The chain starts as a clear set of solid links, then dissolves into a smeary, liquid-like blur that loses its link structure and seems to merge with the arm. By the end it reappears as a separate chain alongside a ghostly translucent shape, so the object does not stay consistent.

The person exhales smoke for about 2.2 seconds with no pipe in view. The pipe then appears at his mouth out of nowhere from about 2.96 s, which is the wrong order of events. The exhaled smoke behaves fairly naturally, but the pipe appearing is an object-permanence glitch.

The child swings the hammer and it seems to strike the top of the toy cage at around 2.3 s, yet the toy never reacts or falls. The cage's internal parts also shift and morph oddly, and the hammer seems to pass through or merge with the top.

The boat moves left, but a rigid red pole sticks out of its stern with tow lines trailing behind, and no skier is ever seen being pulled. The spray plume runs along the line instead of coming off the hull's wake, which is not how real water spray behaves. Buoys and the background also shift oddly.

A farmer picks raspberries and puts them into a crate. The hand motions and berry handling look mostly plausible, with possible small inconsistencies: the crate shifts position slightly, and the berries in the farmer's hand appear and disappear somewhat ambiguously. There are no clear violations.

The video shows a static wooden dowel with an already splintered end resting on a surface. Across the frames only a slight camera drift is visible, and nothing physically implausible happens, though no breaking action occurs either.

The number of balls keeps changing: three, then one, then two, then four objects at 5.00 s, some of which look like fragments. The balls also appear and disappear without matching the hand motions, and some seem to hover beside the hands rather than resting in them.

The seed head starts out partly bald, with a bare center, but it grows fuller over time and ends up a complete puffball even though seeds keep flying away. That is reversed seed release, effectively seeds reappearing on the head.

Only one ball appears, and it hovers around the player's head and shoulder for about four seconds. It drifts slowly sideways and downward without being visibly struck and without falling under gravity, so it looks like it is levitating.

The ball sits on the table, the paddle presses down over it and the ball vanishes beneath the paddle. It then reappears behind the paddle and floats upward slowly with no clear strike. Its size and position change inconsistently, so the impact makes no physical sense.

Hands hold a small tool over a folded paper rosette. The hand motions are subtle and the paper stays mostly stable. Toward the end the tool and fingers blend together oddly, and the white tip looks somewhat ambiguous, with slight morphing of the tool shape.

The gymnast's body changes discontinuously: in the first frames she has a black leotard and bare legs, then she suddenly has full black sleeves and leggings. At 1.46 s a stray leg/foot appears floating in the background. She holds a handstand far too long for a back handspring, and at the end she floats mid-air in an inverted pose with her hands off the floor and no clear push-off. Body parts merge, and the motion doesn't follow the momentum of a real handspring.

The bow tie is already fully formed and never changes in a way that tying could cause. Thin red strings appear and vanish below it, the bow reshapes from frame to frame, and the hands pinch at nothing, so the fabric is not actually being manipulated. The bow keeps transforming without any real interaction.

Two hands fiddle with the laces of a black sneaker in small, steady motions. The shoe and hands stay consistent, but the laces never visibly form a knot or bow, and the hand-lace contact looks somewhat ambiguous. Nothing clearly breaks physics, though.

The camera slowly pans along a static wall-bar structure, and an athlete then appears performing a dip-like movement. In the last frames, the athlete's body seems to merge with or pass through the bars, so the bar geometry and the body interaction are somewhat implausible.

The tool keeps changing shape, from a short knife-like pruner into long loppers, and a gnarled branch with roots attached disappears between 1.42 s and 2.12 s without ever being cut. The blade then sits on the branch for the rest of the clip with no cut and no snap.

The bowl rocks back and forth on the cloth but never falls onto its side. It holds tilted poses that look unstable, such as resting partly on its rim at 0 s and 4.42 s, and it seems to morph and shift without a clear cause.

The foreground dandelion head stays full while seeds appear from nowhere. It then vanishes or turns into a blurry clump at the bottom of frame, and the background head moves forward and stays intact. The seeds float in odd orientations and some spontaneously appear or disappear, so the release from the seed head is not physically consistent.

The debris pile and broken chunks keep resetting between swings, appearing, disappearing and reappearing, while fragments seem to hang in mid-air on the wall. The sledgehammer's grip and position also change inconsistently, for example held by the head near the body at 1.46 s, so the destruction does not build up the way real damage would.

The chocolate poured into the saucer turns into a white, reflective surface instead of a brown pool. Afterward the mug sits on the table full again even though it was just emptied, and a glass jug is never put down. So the liquid amounts and the objects are not consistent from frame to frame.

The ball sits inside the net held by a player's hand. Then a second ball appears in midair below the hoop while the net is empty, and the ball later shows up in another player's hand above the rim. Players and the ball appear and vanish between frames, so there is no continuous trajectory.

A hand holds a bottle and pushes it down into a pocket. The bottle stays roughly in place, the fabric deforms modestly, and the hand releases it smoothly. There is mild morphing of the pocket and the hand-bottle contact, but nothing clearly impossible.

The 'loppers' are a single stick with no blades, and they never actually cut anything. Foliage morphs and blurs, the tool changes length and appears to slide through the bush, and no branch is cleanly severed or falls as a cut branch should.

The faucet's water stream switches on and off without anyone touching the tap, and the sponge's shape and size change in ways that don't match how it is being squeezed. Water also falls from odd places that don't line up with the sponge being wrung.
